# ARC

1. It is an autumn afternoon at the Ranch Stella d'Oro, and Noe takes two tin stars out of the wagon box, pins one on Lio and one on Noam, and says the ride leaves as soon as the wagon is loaded; Elena swings the last crate up and says nobody rides before she has counted every rider; Saba says a good ride needs a good story. Lio rubs his star on his sleeve until it shines properly.

2. Sara brings a basket of apples for the ride and gives one to Noam for Léon, so Noam holds it out flat on his palm at the paddock fence, but Léon's mouth is big and Noam pulls his hand back and puts the apple in his pocket; Lio feeds Léon instead. Noam feels small.

3. Anna comes down the track with Nalu, who pulls hard and barks at a magpie sitting in the chestnut tree by the ditch, so Anna holds her and says the mist is already lying in the low field.

4. The paddock gate hangs open and Léon is gone; Anna says he lifts the latch with his lips, therefore Lio says out loud that they must find Léon before the mist fills the field, because a place where he can see nobody at all is the thing he hates most.

5. Anna scrapes the last oats out of the sack into the tin bucket, shakes the sack upside down until nothing falls, and says Léon always comes to that rattle; she gives the bucket to Noam.

6. Anna hangs Léon's lead rope over Lio's arm and says Léon comes home on the rope, but the boys keep a hand on the fence rail, and Noam does not climb the open steps of the Ponticello del Salice, because they are metal and he is too small; Lio says he will bring Léon in himself, and Anna waits at the gate with the others and the loaded wagon.

7. Noam walks with the bucket along the rail, but he sees a chestnut shining in the wet leaves under the tree, therefore he lets go of the rail and stoops for it while the mist thickens.

8. Lio turns round and sees nobody, so he is alone in the white and he is frightened, and he calls and calls until Noam rattles the bucket and comes back to him; Lio takes his hand and holds it.

9. The bucket tipped while Noam ran, therefore the oats lie in the ditch water, and the sack at the ranch is empty, so the sound that calls Léon is gone; Lio wanted this done neatly and now he is cross.

10. Under the chestnut tree the magpie scolds them, Nalu lunges for her, so the boys hold her collar and see the hoard in the hole of the trunk — Anna's spoon, a buckle, a bottle cap — and they leave every shiny bit where it is.

11. Noam fills the empty bucket with fallen chestnuts and shakes it, therefore it rattles almost like oats, and far off past the ditch Léon answers.

12. Léon stands on the far side of the shallow ditch beyond the little bridge, but Noam must stay off the open steps, so he holds Nalu and keeps rattling; Lio is afraid to go over alone into the mist, therefore he goes anyway, one hand on the rail, one slow step at a time.

13. The magpie drops out of the grey straight at Lio's shining star and Léon throws up his head and backs away, and Lio waves her off but she comes straight back, therefore Lio understands what she came for, unpins his star and lays it on the fence post, and she carries it off to her tree.

14. Léon does not come a second time for chestnuts, so Lio walks out into the mist to him, says his name, clips the rope to the halter, and leads him back over the bridge in front, by himself, to the gate where Elena counts two boys, one dog and one horse; Lio is not afraid now, he is proud.

15. Léon reaches for the gate latch with his lips and Noam pushes the gate shut on him, the mist slides off the field and the towers of Castelgrande stand above it, therefore the ride can go; Noam takes the apple out of his pocket, holds it flat on his palm, and Léon takes it, so Noam shouts "Yee-haw!" while the magpie sits on the gatepost with a star that shines.
